垣.meaning: A burger lover plants a row of bushes in the <part>soil</part> round his garden and clips them into a giant <part>burger</part>: leafy lettuce, a round bun on top, even white flowers for sesame seeds. The neighbours can't see in, only smell his barbecue. It's the tastiest <kanji>hedge</kanji> in town.
垣.on: He trims it with roaring clippers driven by a tiny <sound>en</sound>gine.
垣.kun: A gate shaped like a <sound>car</sound>p opens only with a brass <sound>key</sound>.

批.meaning: A pirate captain drops <part>anchor</part> beside a floating café and tastes the soup with <part>two spoons</part> at once, frowning. 'Too salty. Too wet. Too much soup.' The chef sobs into his apron. The captain is famous for harsh <kanji>criticism</kanji>.
批.on: The chef stamps his <sound>hee</sound>l on the deck and throws the pot overboard.

詳.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> is asked how her day went and gives a three-hour <part>speech</part>: every blade of grass she chewed, every cloud, the exact number of times the farmer sneezed. The flock falls asleep standing up. Her report is very <kanji>detailed</kanji>.
詳.on: Next year she turns it into a stage <sound>show</sound> with slides.
詳.kun: The farm <sound>coo</sound>k says it's a <sound>wo</sound>nder anyone stays awake.

枝.meaning: A lumberjack's daughter won't let him cut down the old <part>tree</part>, so she climbs up, ties a hammock to its lowest <part>branch</part> and moves in with a kettle and a cat. He gives up. Now the family has a guest room on a <kanji>bough</kanji>.
枝.on: She props an old knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld against the trunk as her front door.
枝.kun: Every morning she fries an <sound>e</sound>gg for her pet <sound>du</sound>ck, up on the branch.

君.meaning: A parrot works the front desk of a grand hotel. It grips a <part>baton</part> in one claw to tap the bell, then opens its <part>mouth</part> and greets every guest the same way: 'Good evening, sir!' The dog, the toddler, the duchess: to the parrot, everyone is <kanji>mister</kanji>.
君.on: One guest arrives wrapped up in a silk co<sound>coon</sound>, and the parrot bows anyway.
君.kun: It hands each guest a room <sound>key</sound> and sends a <sound>mee</sound>rkat bellhop to carry the bags.

康.meaning: A janitor finally retires to a garden <part>shed</part>. He leans his old <part>mop</part> in the corner, puts his feet up and has nothing to clean but his teacup. After a month the bored mop sprouts daisies. He has found his <kanji>ease</kanji>.
康.on: Each afternoon he sits in the doorway licking an ice cream <sound>cone</sound>, very slowly.

洞.meaning: Twin fox cubs, the <part>same</part> down to the last whisker, dig a hideout behind a waterfall, where a curtain of <part>water drops</part> hides the way in. Their mum can never tell which one sneaked out at night. It's the perfect <kanji>den</kanji>.
洞.on: They line the floor with big lumps of bread <sound>dough</sound> for pillows, warm and squishy.
洞.kun: A bat lodging in the roof shares his <sound>ho</sound>tdog and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men with them.

暇.meaning: On her day off, a firefighter climbs a <part>rope ladder</part> to her roof and lies in the <part>sun</part> with a lemonade, ignoring the phone ringing below. The cat climbs up to join her. Nothing to do but nap: pure <kanji>spare time</kanji>.
暇.on: From the roof she dangles a line into the pond and teases a big orange <sound>car</sound>p.
暇.kun: She lets one bare <sound>hee</sound>l hang over the edge, and a <sound>ma</sound>ma pigeon perches on it.
